name: Mr Morris Kizito Mukasa
role: Chief Executive Officer, KWETU CONNECT PTY LTD
photoAlt: Portrait of Mr Morris Kizito Mukasa

blocks.text: Mr Morris Kizito Mukasa is a Ugandan-born Australian citizen, humanitarian, distinguished community leader and international advocate whose work spans social justice, cultural integration, trauma recovery, refugee support and the empowerment of marginalised communities.

With extensive experience across different continents, Morris has dedicated his professional and community engagements to addressing social barriers, promoting intercultural understanding, resolving conflicts and developing practical responses to the challenges facing vulnerable populations.

He is particularly recognised for championing the preservation and integration of cultural values, traditional knowledge and indigenous wisdom into contemporary approaches to community development, social cohesion and human wellbeing. His philosophy places particular emphasis on what he describes as "Forgotten Cultural Values" – the rediscovery and application of cultural traditions, principles and practices that risk being overlooked or lost in modern society.

Through his work, he seeks to transform cultural diversity into an asset, social challenges into opportunities, and community knowledge into practical solutions for governments, churches, universities, researchers and diverse communities.

chapters.title: Humanitarian work and community leadership

blocks.text: In Australia, Morris is a co-founder of Kwetu 4 Communities Inc., a non-profit association committed to promoting cultural understanding, social inclusion and trauma healing.

Through its flagship Kwetu Projects, the organisation has supported refugees, asylum seekers, detainees and other vulnerable populations. Its approach incorporates music, creative arts, cultural performances and intercultural dialogue as complementary tools for therapeutic engagement, community healing and social reconnection.

His work also extends to refugee advocacy and pastoral support through leadership and engagement with the Refugee Communities Advocacy Network (RCAN), including the National Catholic Immigrants and Refugees Chaplaincy Office and ACMRO.
His wider community leadership engagements include:

items: Board Member, The Global Talent Pathways.
Board Member, Refugee Communities Advocacy Network (RCAN).
Committee Member, CICT, New South Wales, Australia.
Engagement in national and international refugee advocacy and community representation initiatives.

chapters.title: Catholic Church and cultural heritage engagement

blocks.text: Morris has a longstanding interest in the intersection of faith, cultural identity, community protection and social responsibility.
His areas of engagement include Mission After Custody chaplaincy and the protection and safeguarding of Catholic Church land and property interests through land inspection and related initiatives.

He is also recognised for advancing ideas around cultural inculturation – the meaningful integration of cultural identity, indigenous wisdom and traditional values into contemporary religious, social and institutional settings.

In 2026, he was nominated to represent African Culturally and Linguistically Diverse (CALD) communities in the Synod of the Archdiocese of Sydney, contributing to discussions and guidance concerning the Catholic Church and its diverse communities.

chapters.title: Policy advocacy, conflict resolution and international engagement

blocks.text: Throughout his career, Morris has contributed to policy advocacy, community conflict resolution and international dialogue.

His engagements have included interaction with international institutions and representatives, including participation in dialogues involving the International Criminal Court (ICC) and United Nations representatives in Australia, particularly in relation to refugee support, human rights and community concerns.
His work focuses on identifying barriers affecting vulnerable populations, facilitating constructive engagement among stakeholders and developing practical, culturally informed solutions.
His professional interests encompass:

items: Social justice and human rights advocacy.
Cultural heritage preservation and intercultural dialogue.
Mental health awareness and culturally responsive approaches.
Community policy development and institutional engagement.

chapters.teaser: Dialogue with international institutions and practical solutions

chapters.title: Corporate leadership and international consultancy

blocks.text: Morris is the Chief Executive Officer of KWETU CONNECT PTY LTD, an Australian consultancy focused on navigating cultural, social and economic barriers while creating opportunities for sustainable development.
The consultancy's areas of interest include cultural heritage, health equity, sustainable trade, community resilience and mental health challenges.

Its approach incorporates the recruitment and engagement of relevant professionals alongside complementary cultural approaches, particularly the rediscovery and application of forgotten cultural values.
Morris also serves as the African Regional Consultant for INSULTEC, bringing regional knowledge and cross-cultural engagement to its wider consultancy interests.
Additionally, he represents Integrated Systems USA in a consultancy capacity and is associated with the GLOTADALS 2026 Programme, covering Eastern and Southern Africa and Oceania.

chapters.title: African heritage, kingdom diplomacy and economic development

blocks.text: Morris maintains strong links with his Ugandan heritage and the wider African diaspora.

In 2020, he was appointed to promote the Kabaka Foundation of the Kingdom of Buganda in Australia, supporting the visibility and engagement of Buganda's cultural and institutional heritage within the Australian environment.
His work recognises the importance of traditional institutions, cultural leadership and indigenous knowledge in strengthening community identity and international cooperation.

In 2026, he was appointed the inaugural President of the Australia African Nations Business Council, a leadership role directed towards strengthening engagement between African nations and Australia through business cooperation, trade, investment and institutional partnerships.

chapters.teaser: The Kabaka Foundation and the Australia African Nations Business Council

blocks.text: In recognition of his contribution to community service and humanitarian engagement, Morris received the African Australian Community Service Award (2024).
This recognition reflects his commitment to community empowerment, cultural understanding, refugee support and the promotion of social inclusion.

chapters.title: Guiding philosophy and legacy

blocks.text: Morris Kizito Mukasa's work is founded on the conviction that cultural identity, indigenous wisdom and forgotten community values are important resources for addressing contemporary social challenges.

He advocates for a world in which cultural diversity is embraced as a source of strength, traditional knowledge is respected alongside modern expertise, and vulnerable communities are empowered to participate meaningfully in decisions affecting their lives.

His enduring ambition is to build bridges between Africa and the international community, between traditional institutions and modern governance, and between humanitarian ideals and practical solutions.
